program_name: Planning and Management of Tourism Systems (PMTS)
degree_class: LM-49 (Planning and management of tourism systems)
programme_name_history: The current programme site uses the abbreviation PMTS. The supplied legacy URL uses the PGST subdomain, while the current official programme site is ls-pmts.unibg.it. No substantive former degree title was verified. [uncertain]
admission_type: Open access with verification of curricular requirements and a compulsory assessment of personal preparation; the programme organises an interview with teaching staff.
academic_requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree, a three-year university diploma, or a suitable foreign qualification. Direct curricular eligibility applies to Italian degrees in classes L-15, L-12, L-11, L-1, L-3 and L-13. Holders of other Italian degree classes must have at least 40 CFU across the specified relevant disciplinary sectors. Curricular requirements must be satisfied before personal-preparation assessment; missing requirements cannot be replaced by educational debts/OFA. Foreign-degree holders are evaluated under current rules and the programme's academic regulations by a programme commission.
curricular_requirements_cfu: For Italian degrees outside L-15, L-12, L-11, L-1, L-3 and L-13: at least 40 CFU acquired in the programme's characterising/related areas, namely SECS-P/08; M-GGR/01 and M-GGR/02; L-ART/04 and L-ART/06; SPS/10; L-LIN/04, L-LIN/07 and L-LIN/14; and SECS-P/06, L-LIN/10, M-DEA/01, IUS/04 and IUS/14. English must additionally be evidenced by at least 9 CFU in L-LIN/12 or an equivalent B2 certificate.
entry_exam_or_test: No competitive entrance examination is stated. A compulsory interview/test verifies initial preparation after curricular eligibility is checked. The programme-specific interview examines the applicant's background in sustainable tourism according to WTO principles and English fluency.
interview_required: Yes. The programme page states that an interview with teaching staff will be organised to analyse sustainable-tourism background, English fluency and confirm admission. For 2026/27, general open-access MA interview windows are 2026-06-22 to 2026-06-26, 2026-09-10 to 2026-09-18, and 2026-10-14 to 2026-10-20; the PMTS-specific page says the next exact interview date will be published soon. Non-EU applicants who completed the DreamApply pre-assessment interview are excluded from repeating it.
selection_scoring: No numerical scoring rubric or threshold is published on the programme admission page. The teaching staff assesses sustainable-tourism background following WTO principles, English fluency, and suitability for admission. [uncertain]
degree_completion_deadline: Applicants with a foreign qualification who have passed all examinations but have not yet received the bachelor's diploma may use DreamApply if they will obtain the diploma by June 2026; the programme page also permits an official certificate stating the expected graduation date. [uncertain]
application_channel: Applicants with foreign bachelor's degrees use the UniBG DreamApply portal for online pre-evaluation (up to two programme applications). Successful applicants must then complete UniBG pre-enrolment through the Online Students' Helpdesk; non-EU applicants residing abroad and requiring a visa must also complete Universitaly pre-enrolment by 2026-09-30.
language_requirements: Good written and spoken English at CEFR B2 is required. The PMTS curricular rule accepts at least 9 CFU in L-LIN/12 or an equivalent certificate (examples: FCE, TOEFL 72, IELTS 5.5). The DreamApply programme page lists accepted B2 certificates and permits a formal Medium of Instruction certificate; unofficial certificates and self-declarations are not accepted. Native English speakers are exempt from submitting an English certificate or MOI.
accepted_english_certificates: TOEFL iBT: 79-95 (the PMTS academic requirement page also gives TOEFL 72 as an equivalent B2 example)
Cambridge First Certificate: grades B or C
Pearson Test of English General: Level 3
TIE: minimum B2 in both oral and written tests
ESB ESOL International: minimum Pass with Merit
language_waiver_conditions: A formal Medium of Instruction certificate issued by the registrar or international office of the home university is accepted where the completed degree was taught entirely in English. Native English-speaking students are exempt. Unofficial certificates and self-declarations are not accepted.
application_deadline_eu: For EU applicants with a foreign degree, the 2026/27 DreamApply pre-evaluation calls closed on 2026-01-15 (first call, free-access MAs) and 2026-01-31 (second call). Subsequent UniBG open-access MA pre-enrolment deadlines are 2026-05-29, 2026-08-28 and 2026-09-30; late pre-enrolment may be available with a late fee through 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-13 under the published conditions.
application_deadline_non_eu: For non-EU applicants with a foreign degree, the 2026/27 DreamApply pre-evaluation calls closed on 2026-01-15 (first call, free-access MAs) and 2026-01-31 (second call). Non-EU applicants residing abroad and requiring a visa must subsequently complete both UniBG and Universitaly pre-enrolment by 2026-09-30.

application_call_round.round: DreamApply first call (foreign qualifications; free-access MAs)
DreamApply second call (foreign qualifications; free- and limited-access MAs)

results_notification_date: DreamApply first-call ranking: by 2026-03-31; second-call ranking: by 2026-04-30. Later ordinary pre-enrolment outcomes follow the published interview/enrolment calendar; no separate PMTS result dates were found. [uncertain]
max_programme_choices: Up to two Master's degree programmes. DreamApply permits up to two applications; ordinary UniBG pre-enrolment also permits up to two programmes, with a separate EUR 52 fee for each programme.
required_documents: Copy of the bachelor's degree, translated into English or Italian
Official academic transcript for the last three/four years translated into English or Italian, or Diploma Supplement
Descriptions of major-area courses, including relevant contents, themes, aims and objectives
Accepted English B2 certificate or eligible formal Medium of Instruction certificate
If graduating later, an official university certificate stating the expected graduation date
course_descriptions_required: Yes. The online pre-evaluation requires descriptions of major-area courses listing relevant contents, themes, aims and objectives.
application_fee: EUR 30 DreamApply pre-evaluation fee for 2026/27, according to the official international pre-evaluation page.
pre_enrolment_fee: EUR 52 for each selected Master's degree programme; the amount is also due after DreamApply pre-evaluation.
enrolment_deposit: The DreamApply programme page states a non-refundable EUR 156 one-time enrolment fee payable upon arrival in Italy. The current 2026/27 general fee rules separately describe regional tax and stamp duty; the exact final matriculation amount can depend on ISEEU. [uncertain]
tuition_or_fees_link: https://en.unibg.it/study/enrollment/costs/taxes-and-benefits — for 2026/27, comprehensive tuition is income-linked through ISEEU/ISEEU parificato and also varies by study area, enrolment year and full-/part-time status. Published in-course ranges are EUR 200-1,883 (Area 1), EUR 200-1,983 (Area 2), and EUR 200-2,083 (Area 3), plus regional tax and stamp duty. PMTS's exact area was not explicitly verified on the cited page. [uncertain]
tuition_income_linked: Yes. The comprehensive contribution is calculated using ISEEU, degree-course area, years enrolled relative to normal duration, and full-time/part-time status. Students with foreign income use an equivalent ISEEU (ISEEU parificato).

source_quotes.quote: An interview with the teaching staff will be organised, in order to analyse the students' background on sustainable tourism following WTO principles, their fluency in English and to confirm the admission to the course.

Graduates of Italian universities with qualifications other than the aforementioned Italian Degree Classes are required to have acquired at least 40 credits in the fields of the characterizing disciplines.

Good spoken and written knowledge of English is also required (sector L-LIN/12), corresponding to level B2 of the European certification, attested by the acquisition of at least 9 credits or equivalent certifications.
From November 24th 2025 to January 15th 2026: prospective students can apply
From January 1st 2026 to January 31st 2026: prospective students can apply

Compulsory documents for the online pre-evaluation: 1 – Copy of the Bachelor degree translated into English or Italian. 2 – Either copy of the official Academic transcript of the last three/four years translated into English/Italian language or Diploma supplement

For the 2026–2027 academic year, the minimum and maximum amounts of the comprehensive contribution are as follows: Enrolled within standard duration (in-course) AREA 1: from €200 to €1,883; AREA 2: from €200 to €1,983; AREA 3: from €200 to €2,083.

uncertainty_notes: Verified primarily against official UniBG pages carrying 2026/27 information. The PMTS programme page currently says its next exact interview date will be published soon, so only university-wide open-access MA interview windows can be reported. DreamApply displays two expired 2026/27 application buttons but does not expose their dates in the fetched programme page; dates are taken from UniBG's official international pre-evaluation page. The legacy ls-pgst subdomain and current ls-pmts subdomain coexist. The exact PMTS tuition area and the composition of the EUR 156 arrival payment were not explicitly verified.
source_access_status: Official UniBG sources only. The PMTS programme and DreamApply pages were directly accessible through indexed page content. Some central www.unibg.it pages returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch, so their current content was verified through official-domain search-index excerpts; the official en.unibg.it international admission and deadline pages were indexed with full relevant text.
